title: Quench Tower
model_title: Quench Tower (Down-Flow Spray Quench of Hot Gas)

introduction.definition: A quench tower cools a hot gas stream very quickly by spraying water or a recirculated liquid into it. As the fine droplets evaporate, they absorb heat, so the gas drops to near its adiabatic saturation temperature within a short distance. Excess liquid collects in the sump and is recirculated.
applications: Incinerator and thermal oxidizer off-gas before scrubbers/filters
key_points: Limits dioxin re-formation window in incineration
introduction.summary: A quench tower rapidly cools a hot gas stream by spraying water (or a recirculated liquid) into it. Evaporation of the droplets absorbs heat so the gas cools to near its saturation temperature within a short distance, protecting downstream scrubbers and filters.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Gas temperature vs distance falls steeply under the sprays and levels off near adiabatic saturation.

temperature.title: Gas temperature falls rapidly under the sprays
temperature.description: Hot gas (e.g. several hundred °C from an incinerator or reactor) is cooled within a short distance to near its adiabatic saturation temperature as the spray water evaporates. Rapid quenching protects downstream equipment and limits the time spent in the temperature window where dioxins/furans can re-form (roughly 200–400 °C) in waste incineration.

foundation: Vertical vessel on legs/skirt; allow for wet weight and thermal growth; corrosion-resistant materials or linings.
alignment: Level the unit (or set the specified slope for drainage); leave tube-bundle pull-out space equal to the bundle length.
piping: Connect nozzles without forcing (check allowable nozzle loads); fit vents at high points and drains at low points on both sides.
Steam-heated units: install a steam trap or level-controlled drain and a vacuum breaker so condensate cannot back up.
commissioning: Hydro-test both sides per code; vent air; introduce the cold fluid first, then the hot fluid gradually to avoid thermal shock.

routine.task: Check spray pressure, sump level and outlet temperature.

overhaul.task: Inspect lining at the wet–dry zone.

safety: Emergency quench water supply on loss of pumps (protects downstream equipment); hot gas hazards.

video_tutorials.title: Quench Tower — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Quench Tower.
A quench tower cools a hot gas stream very quickly by spraying water or a recirculated liquid into it.
As the fine droplets evaporate, they absorb heat, so the gas drops to near its adiabatic saturation temperature within a short distance.
Excess liquid collects in the sump and is recirculated.
Typical applications include incinerator and thermal oxidizer off-gas before scrubbers/filters; sulphuric acid and chemical plants; cooling gas before baghouses.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Tower Shell (corrosion-resistant), Recirculation Pump, Recirculation Pump — Shaft & Coupling (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Quench Tower — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Quench Tower.
Check spray pressure, sump level and outlet temperature.
Inspect nozzles for plugging/erosion.
Inspect lining at the wet–dry zone.
Watch for nozzle plugging: outlet temperature high. Common cause: solids in recirculated liquid.
Watch for corrosion at wet–dry line: leaks, lining failure. Common cause: acid condensation, chlorides.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
